title: Break a 28-day option into weekly pieces: theta versus gamma
summary: A 28-day at-the-money Nvidia call costs about $10; a weekly costs about $5. Split into weeks, the first week decays about 13% of the price, the second about 16%, and the last week about 50%. That suggests always selling weeklies, but gamma is the price of theta. If implied stays above realized, weeklies win; if realized ends above implied, monthlies smooth the risk.

steps.caption: Nvidia trades near $180. A 28-day at-the-money call costs about $10; a weekly about $5.
The at-the-money strike, where theta and gamma are largest.
Theta speeds up near expiry: about 13% of the price decays in week one, 16% in week two, 50% in the last week.
Gamma rises in mirror image. The fast decay of weeklies is paid for with gamma risk.
High gamma means delta swings fast near the strike, so a sharp move hurts a short weekly.
Which wins depends on volatility: implied above realized favors weeklies; realized above implied favors monthlies.

takeaways: A 28-day option decays slowly at first and fastest in its last week.
Gamma is the price of theta: fast decay comes with large gamma risk.
Sell weeklies only if you expect implied to stay above realized; otherwise monthlies smooth the P&L.
caveats: The speaker promotes a waitlist for his tools; this is promotional.
The decay percentages are from the speaker's table and are not verified. The $180 price is an example matching a $10 option.
